subject.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing

question: Should builtin memory stores become shared by workspace by default, and what migration plus per-agent/session/extraPaths visibility boundary must ship with that change?
rationale: The code choice changes persistent memory ownership and privacy boundaries; automation cannot safely decide whether same-workspace agents should share sessions and extraPaths without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep per-agent default for now
options.body: Preserve current per-agent stores unless a separate approved shared-index design includes migration, filtering, and live proof.

options.title: Adopt shared stores with filters
options.body: Proceed only after adding agent/session/path ownership metadata, search filters, watcher ownership, and a tested doctor migration.

options.title: Defer this PR to the design issue
options.body: Close or pause this branch and keep the source-keyed shared-index discussion on the canonical issue until the boundary is settled.

recommendation.title: Keep per-agent default for now
recommendation.body: Preserve current per-agent stores unless a separate approved shared-index design includes migration, filtering, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision touches the per-agent SQLite migration and memory store ownership work authored in recent history.
